minutes.headline: Architect's preliminary TC Passios renovation estimate came in near $21 million; committee asked for cost-cutting options.
minutes.summary: The TCP Building Design Committee heard site plan updates and the architect's first preliminary construction estimate, which drew sticker shock from members. The architects were asked to return with a list of savings options, and the next meeting was set for Feb 17. The committee also approved Dec 17 minutes, discussed a letter to the select board, building naming, and heard one resident on timing and debt.

public_comment.topic: Thanked committee; shocked by the cost, concerned about the tight timeline to town meeting, debt service under the debt cap, and Turkey Hill costs to follow; suggested possibly not bringing the project to town meeting or widening scope.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of December 17th as presented.

what_happened.line: The committee heard the architect's first preliminary construction estimate for the renovation and asked for a list of cost-saving options with price impacts.
The architect walked through the estimate by division, then added contingencies, contractor overhead and profit, bond and escalation to reach the total.
The architect said comparable new-construction projects came in at similar or higher cost per square foot than the renovation.
A revised cost estimate is due to the committee by Feb 12, and the next meeting is set for Wednesday Feb 17.
The chair will draft a letter to the select board for committee review, and a public forum is targeted for mid-March.

why_it_matters: The estimate is the first look at what the renovation may cost, and any amount put to Town Meeting would likely be paid through borrowing, which adds to future tax bills.
One resident raised how the annual debt payments would fit under the town's debt cap alongside other projects expected to borrow, so this project may compete with them for room.
